text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection rollout yesterday I'm seeing slow steady memory growth on long-context replay workloads when continuous batching merges many prefixes. Repro on staging. :thinking_face:
ashwin: Can you paste the perf trace? flamegraph or pprof?
dan: probably related to recent KV cache prefetch change + the new merge heuristic. we changed merge_threshold from 12 -> 20 last deploy.
maria: attaching quick snippet of pprof top (trimmed):
```
# top of heap:
11.2% runtime.mallocgc
9.8% kvcache.(*Shard).allocFrag
7.1% kvcache.mergeCandidate.buildMergedView
5.0% continuousbatch.(*Batch).appendKVRef
```

sylvie: interesting — allocFrag + buildMergedView high suggests we're materializing more fragments during merge. do we keep refs instead of shared slices?
ashwin: the new kernel picker also biases for long-seq kernels which increases batch head latency and causes more small merges to queue up. head-of-line blocking -> many merges in parallel -> fragmentation.
maria: repro steps i used: run longctx-replay with batch size 32, concurrency 40, synthetic mix of cache hits/misses (hit ratio ~ 0.75). after ~20m RSS climbs ~600MB.
dan: can you post the exact command?
maria: `./run_replay --profile pprof.pb --bsize 32 --concurrency 40 --seed 17 --kv-prefetch=on`
sylvie: quick idea: when mergeCandidate.buildMergedView copies KV buffers eagerly, we could switch to an mmap-backed read-only view for fragments above threshold to avoid copying. cheap experiment: toggle env KV_COPY_ON_MERGE=0
ashwin: also try limiting the number of concurrent merges with `--merge-parallelism=4` — if head-of-line is the problem, fewer concurrent merges reduces fragment churn.
perf-bot: regression alert: memory_i  +12% in longctx-replay vs previous baseline (job 2026-03-14).
dan: good catch. Does CI perf show the same?
maria: yes, perf job 4018 shows allocation spike correlating with kernel picker change. pprof heap shows many short-lived objects from `kvcache.fragmentIterator.next`
ashwin: hypothesis: merging algorithm creates temporary buffers proportional to merged-depth; continuous batching now merges more shallow but more frequent fragments due to split policy change. two knobs: increase split_threshold to reduce splits, or change merge to reuse fragment slices.
sylvie: i pushed small patch to reuse buffers in branch `kv/reuse-buffer-optim`. local reduces allocs by ~35% in quick run. but need more tests around concurrency and GC pressure.
dan: can we add a dev-profiling flag that dumps merge queue length + frag count every 30s? that'll help correlate with RSS.
maria: i added `KV_DEBUG_DUMP=1` and uploaded the log gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 — shows spikes right before GC sweeps.
ashwin: logs show merge-queue hitting 28, and each merge touching ~12 fragments -> sketch of churn.
sylvie: follow-up experiment plan: 1) roll back kernel picker bias, 2) test `KV_COPY_ON_MERGE=0`, 3) run with `--merge-parallelism=4`, 4) validate `kv/reuse-buffer-optim`.
dan: agree. prioritize the non-invasive flags first (env + merge-parallelism). if that fixes, we can keep kernel change and apply buffer reuse.
maria: I can run a 2h regression on staging with those flags and post traces. starting now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
perf-bot: job queued: longctx-replay-401820-2 (flags: KV_COPY_ON_MERGE=0, MERGE_PAR=4)
ashwin: also add a tiny metric: `kv.merge.copy_bytes_total` so we can measure copy volume.
sylvie: created PR to add metric and a short doc in code comments.
dan: if experiments fail, fallback is to revert kernel picker change; we need to communicate risk to platform.
maria: experiment finished — initial numbers look promising: RSS stable, allocs down ~30%, latency SLO unaffected. uploading traces.
ashwin: awesome. can we get canary on production with MERGE_PAR=4 and KV_COPY_ON_MERGE=0 for 2 hours?
dan: yes, will prepare canary rollout with automatic rollback if mem > baseline + 20%.
sylvie: after canary, follow-up: harden buffer reuse and add unit tests for fragmented view lifecycle.
maria: thanks everyone. filing follow-up ticket with links to traces and PRs. :white_check_mark:
